summary: A relocated DNR lookout above Chewelah, WA, staffed into 1994 and moved whole by crane to the Colville fairgrounds in 2008.

facts.design: DNR flattop live-in cab with catwalk on a 42-ft wooden tower (built 1983)

events.note: First lookout: platform tower and cabin built by the Washington Division of Forestry
Replaced by a 50-ft pole tower with L-6 (7'x7') cab
Replaced by a 40-ft wooden tower with DNR flattop live-in cab
Current 42-ft wooden tower with DNR flattop cab and catwalk
Last staffed during the 1994 fire season per FFLOS
Moved intact ~30 miles to the Colville (Stevens County) fairgrounds after DNR needed the summit for a Homeland Security facility

evidence.supports: near Chewelah, WA; known as Stranger though most maps say Stensgar
evidence.quote: Stranger ("Stensgar" on most maps), a DNR live-in lookout tower near Chewelah, WA
Stensgar Mountain was first used for fire detection in 1930 when a platform tower and cabin were built by the Washington Division of Forestry

evidence.supports: 1936 replacement, 50-ft pole tower with L-6 cab
evidence.quote: The original platform tower was replaced by a 50' pole tower with L-6 cab in 1936

That in turn was replaced by DNR flattop live-in cab with catwalk on a 40' wooden tower in 1959 which only 24 years later was replaced with the current updated DNR flattop cab on a 42' wooden tower in 1983

evidence.supports: cab and catwalk together on the structure that was moved in 2008
evidence.quote: A boom crane, on the mountaintop to install a new Homeland Security facility, was able to pluck the entire cab and catwalk off its 40' wooden tower.
It offers incredible views south across the Columbia Basin and Spokane, east to Montana, west to the Cascade Mountain Range, and north into Canada
was last staffed during the tinder-dry 1994 fire season
the tower was moved to the Northeast Washington Fairgrounds in Colville in 2008

evidence.supports: move by crane after negotiation with DNR
evidence.quote: It had to be removed from the mountain. In a dream-come-true fashion, Stevens County Fair manager Lori Matlock was able to fit the use of nearly a dozen pieces of donated heavy machinery into a fine tuned clockwork that made it all happen.
Total cost: $25. The rest was all donated.

evidence.supports: re-set on concrete piers, crane re-erected it
evidence.quote: The tower's original legs were re-set on concrete piers, cut off at 13'; and a few days later there just happened to be another construction crane available at 4pm. It took but a few minutes, and the Stranger Lookout tower was up in the air again.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR lists the lookout as it was when registered in 2003, while the structure was still on the mountain; the tower was later moved intact to the Colville fairgrounds in 2008 and no longer stands on Stranger Mountain itself, which is why FFLOS and other sources mark the original site as 'gone'

notes_for_editor: The tower record also carries an FFLA-sourced relocation event claiming Stranger Mountain was moved to 'Crystal Ridge' (linked to id us-id-stranger-mountain-at-crystal-ridge, in Idaho). Neither NHLR nor FFLOS mention Crystal Ridge; both describe only the single 2008 move to the Colville fairgrounds. This looks like an FFLA data error (possibly a different lookout sharing the 'Stranger Mountain' name) and is worth a human look before publishing the Crystal Ridge link on this page.
